verdict.rationale: Scribe batch submissions can register notifications.webhook_url with a secret. Zoom then sends an outbound POST when the job finishes, signed with an x-zm-signature HMAC-SHA256 value, so a developer does not need to poll get-status. The docs say only that the webhook fires when the job 'finishes'; they do not explicitly confirm that FAILED, PARTIAL or CANCELED jobs trigger it, and webhooks appear to apply only to batch jobs. missing for 10: explicit documentation that failed, partial or canceled terminal states trigger the callback, the webhook payload schema, retry and delivery guarantees, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, a webhook or callback fires when a job completes or fails, so nothing in my system has to poll

citations.quote: A batch submission can register notifications.webhook_url and a secret to receive an outbound POST when the job finishes.
Zoom signs each request with an x-zm-signature HMAC-SHA256 value and timestamp
Jobs expose QUEUED, PROCESSING, SUCCEEDED, PARTIAL, FAILED, and CANCELED states
